newsitem.title: USA: Good crop, smaller India wheat imports-US attache.
newsitem.headline: Good crop, smaller India wheat imports-US attache.

text.p: Unusually good weather during February and March will allow India to harvest about 64.5 million tonnes of wheat this season and reduce its imports to 3.5 million tonnes, the U.S. agricultural attache in New Delhi said in a report released Monday.
"Production might have been even higher were it not for heavy rains, wind, and hail in early April which caused an estimated 500,000 tonnes of damage across northern India," the attache wrote.
Nonetheless, India could harvest its second-largest crop if the 64.5 million tonne estimate proved true, the attache said.
The report was based in part on field trips to major wheat-growing areas.
The estimate of 64.5 million tonnes of wheat was up 500,000 tonnes from an earlier forecast.

"The 1997/98 import forecast is being scaled back 500,000 tonnes to 3.5 (million tonnes) as procurement prospects are expected to be slightly better than initially forecast, reducing the need to import wheat to augment government stocks under current off take and procurement forecasts."
The attache also said government rice stocks dropped to their lowest April 1 level since 1993.
If off take continued at the current pace, rice stocks could drop to near the prescribed minimum of 6.0 mmt for the first time since 1992, the attache said.
Wheat procurements were estimated at eight million tonnes, slightly higher than a February estimate thanks to the large crop and market prices that are near the procurement price.
"Given the higher production estimate, 1997/98 wheat imports are now forecast at 3.5 (million tonnes), 500,000 below the February forecast," the attache said.
